title: Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: apostate angels received sufficient media yet some were elect, some reprobate — so sufficient grace to all would not prove reprobation only from foresight of final unbelief
pass_a_gloss: In the apostate Angels the truth of this matter appears clearly. God was not only prepared to give unto them media sufficient and necessary unto standing and persevering in Divine obedience, but he gave them: and nevertheless all Theologians confess that among the Angels themselves some were elect, some non-elect or reprobate. If therefore the adversaries could prove that sufficient grace is given unto all and singular men, they would not therefore rightly infer that no one is reprobated except from foresight of final unbelief. For as, sufficient grace being posited as to some designated person, his antecedent predestination is not therefore posited; so neither, the same sufficient grace being posited as to the same person, is his antecedent reprobation therefore denied.
pass_b_english: The apostate angels make this plain. God was not only ready to give them media sufficient and needful to stand and persevere in divine obedience — he gave them. Yet every theologian grants that among the angels some were elect, some non-elect or reprobate. So even if the adversaries could prove sufficient grace is given to every human being, they still could not rightly infer that no one is reprobated except from foresight of final unbelief. Just as positing sufficient grace for a given person does not posit his antecedent predestination, so positing that same sufficient grace does not deny his antecedent reprobation.
source_text: In Angelis apostatis hujus rei veritas liquido apparet. Deus non modo paratus fuit dare illis media sufficientia et necessaria ad standum et perseverandum in obsequio Divino, sed dedit: ac nihilominus omnes Theologi fatentur, inter ipsos Angelos quosdam fuisse electos, quosdam non-electos sive reprobatos. Si igitur adversarii possint evincere, omnibus et singulis hominibus gratiam sufficientem dari, non tamen idcirco recte intulerint, neminem nisi ex praevisione finalis infidelitatis reprobari. Nam sicuti posita gratia sufficiente quoad designatam aliquam personam, non ponitur idcirco antecedanea ejus praedestinatio; ita nec posita eadem gratia sufficiente quoad eandem personam negatur idcirco antecedanea ejusdem reprobatio.
